{"action":"write_file","content":"# Specification Quality Checklist: Tagged Cache (TaggedCache)

**Purpose**: Validate specification completeness and quality before proceeding to planning
**Created**: 2026-10-19
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

## Content Quality

- [x] No implementation details (languages, frameworks, APIs)
  - Note: The spec references the project's existing LRU cache, the module
    path src/cachetools/tagged.py, and the acceptance file
    acceptance_public.py. These are scope/dependency facts taken directly
    from the issue text (required inputs), not design choices made by the
    spec. No language-specific APIs, class internals, or algorithm choices
    are prescribed. The deep-copy semantics are described in terms of the
    standard library's standard deep-copy behavior, which is a reasonable
    default documented in Assumptions rather than an implementation
    directive.
- [x] Focused on user value and business needs
- [x] Written for non-technical stakeholders
- [x] All mandatory sections completed (User Scenarios & Testing, Requirements,
  Success Criteria, Assumptions; Key Entities included because the feature
  involves data)

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] No [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers remain (verified by grep: zero matches)
- [x] Requirements are testable and unambiguous (each FR maps to at least one
  acceptance scenario or edge case with concrete inputs/outputs)
- [x] Success criteria are measurable (SC-001 through SC-006 use counts,
  percentages, and zero-defect statements)
- [x] Success criteria are technology-agnostic (no mention of specific
  frameworks, languages, or internal data structures; SC-005/SC-006 reference
  the project's own test suites as the verification vehicle, which is the
  project's stated acceptance mechanism, not an implementation detail)
- [x] All acceptance scenarios are defined (User Stories 1-3 each carry
  numbered Given/When/Then scenarios; Edge Cases section covers boundary and
  error conditions)
- [x] Edge cases are identified (bare-string tags, nonstring entries, empty
  tags, failure-before-state-change, invalid replacement, recency on
  overwrite and on get, maxsize boundary including bool exclusion, tag
  deduplication, key reuse after eviction, existing API preservation)
- [x] Scope is clearly bounded (new additive class; existing APIs preserved;
  implementation source file named; upstream tests unchanged)
- [x] Dependencies and assumptions identified (existing LRU cache reused;
  standard deep-copy semantics; finite iterable definition; error type
  convention; R02 extension treated as active requirement with documented
  uncertainty; export convention)

## Feature Readiness

- [x] All functional requirements have clear acceptance criteria (FR-001
  through FR-019 each trace to User Story 1-3 scenarios or Edge Cases)
- [x] User scenarios cover primary flows (store/retrieve with isolation,
  tag invalidation, recency and capacity)
- [x] Feature meets measurable outcomes defined in Success Criteria
- [x] No implementation details leak into specification (see Content Quality
  note above)

## Notes

- All items pass on the first validation iteration; no spec updates were
  required.
- One documented uncertainty remains (Assumptions: the R02 extension
  put_no_recency_refresh variant). The spec follows the literal text of the
  extension (overwrite refreshes recency) as FR-014. If a later phase
  determines the variant should suppress the refresh, FR-014 and the related
  acceptance scenarios must be revisited. This is tracked, not a blocker.
- Items marked incomplete would require spec updates before `$speckit-clarify`
  or `$speckit-plan`; none are currently incomplete.
", "path": "specs/001-transactions/checklists/requirements.md"}
